questions.question: What are the three evaluation layers the lesson names?
options: Unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end acceptance test suites
Static benchmarks, custom offline evals, online production evals
Smoke tests, regression tests, and manual acceptance sign-off checks
Pre-stage, check-stage, and post-stage quiz question tags used in this course
questions.explanation: Static (SWE-bench, GAIA), custom offline (LLM-judge, exec, trajectory), online (replays, alerts, cost/latency).

questions.question: What is Anthropic's recommended starting point?
options: Start with multi-agent debate among several specialized subagents before ever writing a single simple baseline prompt to compare
Start with hierarchical orchestration and a planner-executor split before evaluating any single prompt
Start with simple prompts, optimize them with comprehensive evaluation, and add multi-step agentic systems only when needed
Start with a frontier model only and skip evaluation until the agent is already deployed to production
questions.explanation: Anthropic explicitly says evaluation is the outer loop that drives every other choice.

questions.question: What is the evaluator-optimizer tight loop?
options: Train the model, evaluate on a held-out benchmark, then deploy directly to production traffic
Sample many candidate outputs, sort by score, and deduplicate near-identical responses before returning
Cache the first response, retry on any failure, and fail silently after three attempts
Proposer generates output, evaluator judges, refine until evaluator passes (Self-Refine generalized)
questions.explanation: It is Self-Refine generalized: any flow can wrap in propose-judge-refine.

questions.question: What is the 2026 best practice for where evals live?
options: Next to code, run in CI on every PR, gate merges on eval scores
In a separate vendor dashboard only, reviewed manually once a release ships
Only run quarterly during a scheduled review cycle separate from the CI pipeline
Owned exclusively by the QA team, never touched by agent engineers
questions.explanation: Co-located with code, CI-gated, regression-tracked is the standard.

questions.question: Why does the lesson warn against an LLM-judge without grounding?
options: It is too slow to run inside a CI pipeline gating merges on every pull request
Judges hallucinate too; pair with the CRITIC pattern so judgment grounds on external tools
It violates the Apache 2.0 open-source license terms attached to most evaluation frameworks used here
It only works on GPU-backed inference endpoints, not CPU-only judge deployments
questions.explanation: CRITIC (Lesson 5) applies: tool-grounded verification keeps the judge honest.

questions.question: What is the danger of over-fitting to evals?
options: Compute cost rises sharply because every eval run re-invokes the full agent loop and judge model
Vector index fragmentation increases and retrieval latency in the RAG pipeline slowly climbs
Latency drops too far below production SLAs once evals are removed from the CI pipeline
Optimizing for the eval set diverges from production usefulness; rotate cases
questions.explanation: Eval set rotation keeps the optimization aligned with production reality.

questions.question: Why do flaky evals cause problems?
options: Non-deterministic cases produce false alarms; pin seeds and snapshot state
They double inference cost because every flaky case gets retried automatically three times
They cannot reach the database that stores baseline scores for regression comparison
They exceed the context window once trace history from prior runs is appended to the prompt
questions.explanation: Flake makes regressions unreadable; determinism (seeds, state snapshots) is required.
